facts.raw_span: asymptomatic cutaneous lesions on the face that had progressively spread to the trunk and extremities
asthenia and mild intermittent arthralgias
Multiple millimetric erythematous to hyperpigmented monomorphic keratotic papules involving the head, trunk, and extremities
Symmetric annular brown erythematous plaques on the cheeks and temples
No vesicles or pustules
Normal white blood cell count
Mild anemia (hemoglobin level, 11.3 g/dL; normal level 12.50-15.50 g/dL)
Hypocomplementemia
Moderate proteinuria
Raised levels of antinuclear antibodies (>1:160)
Positive: anti-Smith antibodies, SSA/Ro antibodies, SSB/La antibodies, and anti-U1RNP antibodies
Slightly atrophic epidermis with interface dermatitis, individual dyskeratotic keratinocytes, and a superficial perivascular and interstitial infiltrate of neutrophils

concepts.why: The patient's skin lesions, positive anti-Smith antibodies, and raised levels of antinuclear antibodies are consistent with Subacute Cutaneous Lupus Erythematosus.
The patient's skin lesions, mild anemia, and raised levels of antinuclear antibodies are consistent with Discoid Lupus Erythematosus.
The patient's systemic symptoms, positive anti-Smith antibodies, and raised levels of antinuclear antibodies are consistent with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus.
The patient's skin lesions, including erythematous to hyperpigmented monomorphic keratotic papules, are consistent with Psoriasis.
The patient's skin lesions, asthenia, and mild anemia are consistent with Dermatomyositis.
The patient's hypocomplementemia, moderate proteinuria, and superficial perivascular and interstitial infiltrate of neutrophils are consistent with Vasculitis.
The patient's systemic symptoms, positive anti-U1RNP antibodies, and raised levels of antinuclear antibodies are consistent with Mixed Connective Tissue Disease.
The patient's skin lesions, positive SSA/Ro antibodies, and raised levels of antinuclear antibodies are consistent with Sjögren's Syndrome.
